# PRD: Packaged Codex greeting workflow

## Summary
Build two small greeting functions in sequence to prove the installed Kiln package carries real Codex work through two phases and an actual GitHub pull request. Node 22 or later; no external dependencies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-GREETING-01 — A plain greeting.** Export `greeting(name)` from `greeting.js`, returning `Hello, ${name}!` for every string name. Preserve empty strings, Unicode and punctuation verbatim. Verify normal, empty, Unicode and punctuation inputs with Node's built-in test runner.
- [ ] **AC-GREETING-02 — An uppercase greeting.** Export `loudGreeting(name)` from `loud-greeting.js`, calling the first phase's greeting function and returning its result converted with JavaScript `toUpperCase()`. Add tests for normal, empty, Unicode and punctuation inputs; all first-phase tests continue to pass.

## Out of Scope
Merges, deployment, package publication, other repositories, external dependencies and modifications to published method skills. This is a two-phase disposable acceptance proof; whole-PRD audit handoffs are outside this fixture.

# Technical Design: Packaged Codex greeting workflow

**PRD:** [Packaged Codex greeting workflow](codex-packaged-workflow-prd.md).

## Implementation
Phase 1 adds the pure ES module `greeting.js` and `greeting.test.js`, with named export `greeting(name)` using the literal prefix `Hello, ` and suffix `!`. Phase 2 adds `loud-greeting.js`, importing `greeting` and applying `toUpperCase()`, plus `loud-greeting.test.js`. Use Node's built-in `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`; `npm test` runs all tests. No dependency installation is needed.

## Delivery
Use the unchanged installed Enso Method implementation, review, hardening and refactor skills. Each phase closes its own document and commits and pushes to Kiln's assigned feature branch. A separate final conversation opens one actual GitHub pull request. Do not merge, deploy or change another branch. No manual or interruption exercise is needed; earlier real proofs cover those unchanged boundaries.
